summary:
KEYFRAME f1983 (S26, the hand-off frame) is done for 16:9 (2560x1440) and 4:3 (2048x1536). Outside the card it is the live game bit for bit: 0 pixels changed in both buckets.

**Capture.** The live CHRONICA main menu was captured natively at 2560x1440 and 2048x1536 (Playwright Chromium with SwiftShader; fresh profile, so no save and the 5-button card).
- I added a deterministic virtual clock to `capture_menu.mjs`. `performance.now` is frozen inside each browser frame and advances exactly 1/60 s per rAF tick, so Godot runs at a steady 60 fps however slowly SwiftShader renders. FramePace therefore keeps 3D scale at 1.0, and the 3 s camera hold before the tour pans cannot be eaten.
- After callMain the script lets N menu frames run, then holds every rAF callback and screenshots the frozen canvas. Two screenshots of the same frame are bit-identical.
- Menu frames 1 to about 20 still have the city nameplates popping in (larger plates; see `qa/nameplates_popin_mf003_vs_mf030.png`). The keyframe uses menu frame 30: 0.5 s of game time, nameplates settled, camera on its first focus (Grandbois). The frame-3 capture is kept for reference.

**Blank card.** I ported `main_menu.gd _layout()` to Python and reproduced Godot's 2D drawing:
- Control positions are rounded to whole base units; sizes are not.
- TextureRect keep-aspect truncates the fitted size to an int, then centres it.
- Textures use Godot's box mip chain with trilinear filtering; the nine-patch follows canvas.glsl `map_ninepatch_axis`; the bar carries the `WOOD_DARK` modulate.
- Every chrome element then matches the capture to 0.26-0.69/255 mean absolute error.

The card's minimum size, fitted against the captured walnut frame, is **629x665 base units at both scales**, not the 627x661 in `menu_layout.json`. In 16:9 the card is drawn at 224, 318.4, 1006.4x1064 px, and its parchment field is 259.2, 350.4, 936x1000 px. That field is what the S24 leaf has to land on, so the storyboard numbers need updating there.

The card is redrawn from the `menu_card` nine-patch (margins 46/47/48/56). Only the parchment field is replaced: 3 texels inside the inner dark line, 2-texel feather, brass corners excluded. That removes the title, ornaments, subtitle, rule, the 5 buttons and the footer.

**Verification.**

| check | 16:9 | 4:3 |
|---|---|---|
| f1983 vs live frame, outside the card | max 0/255, 0 px changed | max 0/255, 0 px changed |
| rebuilt vs live parchment, content-free areas | 0.48/255 mean | 0.42/255 mean |
| feather band | 0.01/255 | 0.01/255 |

- No seam is visible at 100 % or in the x16 residual.
- G12 outlook (16:9, outside the card, no masks): against live menu frames 3 and 120, f1983 differs by 1.59 and 1.11/255. Both are under 2/255; the differences are only units, water and the nameplate pop-in.
- Reproducibility: a second independent boot matches the first at menu frame 30 except for 334 px (max 25/255). Those are a faint randomly seeded dust puff over unit shields; chrome and card are identical.

**Mattes.** Each element is a full-frame, straight-alpha RGBA layer, per bucket, aligned to the live menu: bar, valance, both banners, both candles, both lions, table edge (4:3 only) and the blank card. There are also composites (`desk_all_but_card`, `chrome_all`), `board_visible_alpha` and the replaced-pixel alpha. Candles (and the 4:3 chamberstick) are also split into flame and unlit (wick only) layers for the unlit and relit desk states. `rects.json` gives rects, draw order, card size and parchment field.

The whole build re-runs with `src/make_all.sh`; `CAPTURE=1` re-captures the live menu first. The README explains everything. I left the static server I started on 127.0.0.1:8765 running (PID 2008) in case other agents need it.
render_cost: Live capture (SwiftShader, headless Chromium, niced): about 60-75 s from boot to callMain, then about 7-10 s per Godot menu frame at 2560x1440, so reaching menu frame 30 takes about 4-6 min wall per bucket. That is 2048x1536 for 4:3; 16:9 menu frame 120 took 15.5 min. Screenshots of the frozen frame take about 2 s each. Compositing (`handoff.py`: card fit, blank card, diff, all mattes and flame splits) takes about 30-35 s per bucket in a single process, below 1.5 GB RSS. Rebuilding everything from the stored captures with `make_all.sh` takes 67 s for both buckets plus the review sheet. Total CPU across the four capture runs (16:9 frames 3/30/120, 4:3 frames 30/60, 16:9 repro) is about 35 min wall. Disk use is 85 MB, including the captures.
self_critique:
I checked all of this on renders I looked at myself: the full frames for both buckets, 100 % crops of all four card corners (16:9 and 4:3), the x8 and x16 difference images, the chrome mattes over a dark checker, and the flame/unlit splits at 2x. Visually the blank card cannot be told from real blank parchment. It is the game's own nine-patch, rebuilt to under 0.5/255 of the live pixels, and nothing outside the card's parchment field changed.

The work went through three iterations:
1. The first rebuild used the documented 627x661 card and unsnapped rects. Right and bottom frame errors were 13-36/255, the bar was off by 18/255, and banners and lions by about 5/255.
2. Fitting showed the card is actually 629x665 base units, and adding the bar's WOOD_DARK modulate fixed the bar.
3. Testing three placement models against the capture showed this Godot build rounds control positions (not sizes) and truncates the keep-aspect size to an int. That brought every element to 0.26-0.69/255.

Where it falls short of the brief:
- The frame is not literally the first menu frame. I chose menu frame 30 (0.5 s) because frames 1 to about 20 show nameplates still popping in. That frame-30 state is what the player sees during the hand-off dissolve, but it is a deliberate deviation, and the frame-3 version can be rebuilt with one command.
- The capture is software WebGL (SwiftShader) in desktop Chromium, not iPad Safari. The 2D chrome and the card are device-independent (Godot draws its own text and art), but the 3D board's sampling and precision may differ on a real iPad GPU. The on-device G12 check in the storyboard is still required.
- The flame/unlit split uses a heuristic mask. A few dark specks of the wick base remain in the flame layers; they are invisible at 1x.
known_issues: menu_layout.json and storyboard section 13 understate the card: the live 5-button card is 629x665 base units, not 627x661, and is drawn from y=199, not 199.18. In 16:9 it is 224, 318.4, 1006.37 x 1063.97 px, and its parchment field (leaf landing) is 259.2, 350.4, 935.97 x 999.97 px. In 4:3 the card is 179.2, 254.72, 805.12 x 851.23 px. Other shots (S22-S26, the PoC leaf landing, G12/G14) should use the numbers in report_*.json / rects.json.

The keyframe is built on live menu frame 30 (0.5 s game time), not frame 1: frames 1 to about 20 show the nameplates popping in at a larger size. That transient differs from f1983 by 1.59/255 mean outside the card (2.1 % of px > 16), still under the G12 2/255 limit.

The captures come from headless Chromium with SwiftShader WebGL2, not iPad Safari's GPU. The 3D board may differ slightly on device, so G12 must still be verified on the shipped encode on device. Units' idle animations, water and tiny random dust puffs are live and differ between frames and boots (repro: 334 px differ, max 25/255).
Only the 16:9 (B169) and 4:3 (B133) buckets were captured. B160, B156, B152 and B143 can be produced with the same scripts (W/H in make_all.sh) once the iPad Safari viewport sizes are measured.
The valance letters and ornaments are kept as live art. Inpainting them for the S24-S26 stitch-on layer was not in scope.
The flame/unlit candle split uses a heuristic texture mask. Tiny dark specks of the wick base remain in the *_flame layers, invisible at 1x.
I left the static file server I started (python3 -m http.server 8765, PID 2008) running for other agents. Stop it when the stage is over.
